item.title: 2026 Year of the Horse: Humans and horses go way back

item.title: Germany news: Crowds throng streets for Carnival parades

item.title: 'No regrets.' Belarusian activist talks exile in Germany

item.title: German and UK military chiefs state case for rearming

item.title: Winter Olympics hit by 'double-touching' curling controversy

item.title: Afraid to go outside? You're not alone

item.title: Prague exhibition documents Slovak National Gallery decline

item.title: France assembles magistrate team to examine 'Epstein files'

item.title: Orban says EU bigger threat to Hungary than Russia

item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy at MSC: Putin is a 'slave to war'

item.title: As the telephone turns 150, are we hanging up on phone calls?

item.title: Amazon cuts more corporate jobs in post-pandemic downsize
item.description: Amazon told employees that it was cutting 16,000 corporate jobs, completing a downsizing move that began last year. The online retail giant had recruited during a COVID pandemic spike in demand.

item.title: Environmental crises add to Iran's mounting troubles
item.description: Widespread discontent in Iran has sent millions of protesters into the streets. Poor environmental planning embodies one of the government's most existential vulnerabilities.

item.title: How Germany's skilled worker gap exposes migration hurdles
item.description: Germany is facing a massive shortage of skilled workers, from nurses to IT specialists. The country needs hundreds of thousands of professionals, but bureaucracy and political hurdles are slowing recruitment abroad.

item.title: What 'banana republic' means — and why its history matters
item.description: From plantations to political rhetoric, the term's evolution shows how a violent past can fade into metaphor, sometimes obscuring its true history.

item.title: FIFA ex-President Blatter backs call to boycott World Cup
item.description: With the US due to co-host the football World Cup this summer, former FIFA President Sepp Blatter said a former colleague was "right" to advise supporters to "stay home" and watch on TV amid an immigration crackdown.

item.title: Plastic emissions could double health damage by 2040
item.description: Plastic pollution could double its harm to human health in the coming decades if current production trends continue, according to a new study that links rising risks directly to the manufacture of new plastics.

item.title: Holocaust survivor Leon Weintraub: "We were dehumanized"
item.description: The 100-year-old vividly recalls the hunger, death camps and cruelty of the guards. Thus, he tirelessly works to ensure that the Holocaust is never forgotten.

item.title: Paris Agreement 10 years on: More wins than you may realize
item.description: Major emitter the US has officially left the Paris Agreement and global emissions keep rising a decade on from the deal. Yet renewables' growth shows climate action can work. Here's what's been done and what's missing.

item.title: Ye aka Kanye West apologizes for antisemitic remarks
item.description: The artist previously known as Kanye West blamed his behavior on bipolar disorder, saying he "lost touch with reality."

item.title: Gold breaks $5,000: What's fueling the price rally and where will it end?
item.description: Gold continues to hit record highs, having already had a bumper run in 2025. Geopolitical and economic uncertainty are the key factors, while doubts over the US dollar are also attracting new investors.

item.title: Germany: Business index starts year with 'little momentum'
item.description: Germany's Ifo business barometer was stagnant in January, bucking predictions of a slight improvement. A dip in confidence in the service sector put the brakes on improved sentiments in other areas.

item.title: EU pushes for deals as Trump's tariffs upset global trade
item.description: Fear over Trump's tariff walls and the aggressive tone coming from the White House is pushing the European Union to focus on getting other trade agreements done. Despite all efforts, the EU sometimes gets in its own way.

item.title: US–EU economic ties show why neither side can decouple
item.description: Despite a pause in tariff escalation, US–EU trade remains volatile under Donald Trump. From deficits and energy to services and the dollar, the trans-Atlantic relationship reveals deep ties — and clear vulnerabilities.

item.title: Germany weighs boon and bane of China's industrial expansion
item.description: From cheap exports to cutting-edge tech: A Chinese battery giant's secretive factory in Germany shows how "Made in China" and "Made in Germany" are colliding — and where they can benefit from each other.

item.title: 'Sweet Caroline' singer Neil Diamond turns 85
item.description: He was a pop icon in the 1970s. Today, one of his songs is experiencing a viral resurgence. From soccer stadiums to TikTok, Neil Diamond's "Sweet Caroline" hasn't stopped playing.

item.title: 'Sinners' breaks records at 2026 Oscar nominations
item.description: The film by Ryan Coogler earned 16 nods for the 98th Academy Awards, which will be presented on March 15. A new Oscar category was also introduced for the first time in 25 years.

item.title: From Inuit to Vikings to Trump: The history of Greenland

item.description: Kurdish Iraqis who survived the 1988 chemical weapons attack on Halabja and nearby communities have lasting trauma, a new report finds, highlighting the need for long-term support.
